commit.message:
fix(ui): steer messages jump into the middle of an active run, then disappear (#165535)

* fix(ui): keep steer messages below already-visible run output

Keep dispatched steers visible once until their canonical transcript copy
arrives, including queued custody, retries, history refreshes, and pane
remounts. Preserve the causal order of live tools and streamed text through
terminal reconciliation.

Persist native assistant prefixes before steering and save only subsequent
text afterward. Track committed segments per mirror candidate so changed
completion identities, repeated steering, and partial-write retries cannot
lose or duplicate the continuation. Reuse the existing transcript schema
and app submission owner.

Cover the queue-strip action, cached projection recovery, stream ordering,
and native transcript persistence with focused regressions.

* test(ui): expect continuation below failed steer

Keep failed-ACK ownership coverage aligned with the dispatched steer boundary. The existing prefix remains visible above the Retry row, while the continuation renders below it and Stop retains the original run target.

Park incoming steering in the existing FIFO owner while its exact reply operation prepares. commit.message:
fix(skills): recheck fresh sessions and retain snapshot providers (#165529)

Fresh sessions re-evaluate prerequisites instead of sharing completed eligibility projections. Existing sessions hydrate only their saved name, path, and host identities before provider precedence is resolved, preserving prompt selection and implementation ownership.

Keep one raw discovery cache and one canonical identity predicate, without parallel source-entry plumbing. Apply that predicate before the node merge and during node name allocation so persisted base names, prefixes, and numeric suffixes survive new local collisions. Retain all six provider-switch cases and the original fresh-session regression; add three node/local collision cases.

Validation: skills and consumer suites passed 1,257 tests with one Windows-only skip across six shards (2317.52 seconds). Focused node and snapshot suites passed 54 tests (96.01 seconds); the new collision regression failed before repair. Independent P0-P2 review is clean.

Changed checks passed production types, all 27 test-type graphs, lint, formatting, and remaining guards. Knip reports inherited unused exports GoogleMeetJoinResult and MeetingRuntimeOwner: definitions, consumers, and scan inputs are unchanged from base f12c30cd91c8f952e573536d9a242da0fb68f850. commit.message:
fix(cron): Codex max thinking drops to default effort on cron and hook turns (#165444)

Codex-harness agents configured with thinking `max` ran at the model's default effort when a cron job or `/hooks` mapping started the turn, while chat and channel turns already used `max`. The isolated cron runner now resolves `max` against the hydrated Codex effort catalog, the same way the interactive paths do. Codex lists `max` as a first-class `ReasoningEffort` (codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models.rs).

Proof: built Gateways with a configured fake Codex app-server that records `turn/start` requests. On a cron run, main sends a null (default) effort and this change sends `max`. Cron `high` stays `high`, and chat-initiated `max` stays `max`, on both. The regression test fails on main and passes here.

Fixes #164812.

* fix(codex): give exec/ALL_TOOLS discovery guidance only to code-mode-only threads

Normal Codex threads received the code-mode-only discovery sentence whenever
any dynamic tool was deferred. Models followed it on ordinary threads: an
exec ALL_TOOLS lookup for a tool already in the direct list, then the direct
call. Thread the effective nativeCodeModeOnlyEnabled flag into the developer
instructions and tell normal threads to call listed tools directly, use
tool_search for unlisted ones, and never re-run a returned tool.

Model metadata can select code-mode-only execution while the configured
flag is false; normal-thread guidance now keeps the exec discovery path for
that case and only forbids exec lookups of tools already in the direct list.

commit.message:
fix: restore managed portals on large Tailscale tailnets (#165507)

On tailnets with many peers, `tailscale status --json` exceeds the 400 KB exec buffer used for hostname discovery. The error was swallowed, so the Gateway never published its hostname and managed portals reported "the managed Tailscale route is not active". Hostname discovery now accepts status output up to 16 MiB, and the `openclaw status` scan uses the same discovery options. A discovery failure now logs a warning while the active Serve/Funnel claim is kept.

Proof: a built Gateway in Docker with a fake `tailscale` returning more than 800 KB of status JSON. Base published no hostname, `status` showed magicdns unknown, and the portal was rejected. With this change the hostname is published, `status` shows it, and `portal.open` succeeds. Small JSON, malformed JSON, a missing binary, and a binary that disappears after the claim all behave as expected. The new regression cases fail on base and pass here.

Fixes #165494.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

commit.message:
test(codex): start parked settlement writes after the deadline jump (#165506)

The terminal settlement timeout cases park a real transcript write behind a
held writer and then jump the fake clock 120 s to the settlement cutoff.
Database worker requests arm their own 60 s timeouts on that fake clock, and
advanceTimersByTimeAsync lets the parked write keep issuing pre-lock worker
reads mid-jump. On a loaded host one expires before the cutoff: the final
mirror resolves unavailable, settlement closes without the drain grace, and
cleanup deadlocks behind the held writer (the checkpoint sibling instead logs
"worker task timed out" and waits for a grace polling never reaches).

Gate the parked real write until after the deadline jump; non-timeout cases
pre-resolve the gate. Recovery abandons the parked checkpoint write and expiry
fences the parked final write, so write ordering is unaffected.

fix(agents): avoid model fallback on local transcript conflicts (#165490)

* fix(agents): keep transcript conflicts out of model retry and fallback

Preserve local transcript conflict identity through the storage worker and agent loop. Keep bounded append recovery at the transcript owner, and surface exhausted conflicts without creating provider failures or replaying model work.

* test(agents): correct transcript worker model fixtures

Remove two misplaced mock arguments introduced while relocating the transcript conflict regression. The complete candidate tree passes 272 focused tests and all selected typecheck graphs.

commit.message:
perf(gateway): avoid placement scans in node retention checks (#165475)

* perf(gateway): avoid placement scans in node retention checks

Reuse the placement owner's worker reads and revocable session observations
for retention publication and dispatch/result authorization. Reject stale
observations while preserving exact environment and manifest ownership,
pending-result protection, ordering, and uniqueness.

Reduce Gateway event-loop stalls as placement inventories grow. Stored data,
configuration, retention policy, and the worker protocol are unchanged.

* test(gateway): prepare node retention fixture once

Build the fixed environment view during fixture setup instead of copying it on every retention read. Keep the placement revocation assertions and store cleanup unchanged.
